content:
Restating primitive as excluding only smaller pairs with \(a\ne b\), we derive the constraints.

From
\[
f^m(x)+f^n(y)=x+y,
\]
subtracting the equation for \(x_1,x_2\) gives
\[
f^m(x_1)-f^m(x_2)=x_1-x_2,
\]
so \(f^m(x)=x+c\). Then
\[
f^n(x)=x-c.
\]
Hence
\[
f^{m+n}=f^m\circ f^n=\operatorname{id}.
\]
Thus \(f\) has finite order, so \(f^m\) has finite order. Since \(f^m(x)=x+c\), we must have \(c=0\). Therefore
\[
f^m=\operatorname{id},\qquad f^n=\operatorname{id}.
\]
Let \(d\) be the order of \(f\). Then \(d\mid \gcd(m,n)\).

Now \(f\) is \((a,b)\)-splendid iff \(d\mid a\) and \(d\mid b\). Write
\[
m=qd,\qquad n=pd.
\]
The possible distinct smaller splendid pairs correspond to off-diagonal pairs \((i,j)\) with \(1\le i\le q,\ 1\le j\le p\). For \((m,n)\) to be primitive, the only off-diagonal pair must be \((q,p)\). This forces
\[
qp-\min(q,p)=1,
\]
so \(\{q,p\}=\{1,2\}\). Thus \((m,n)\) is primitive iff one of \(m,n\) is twice the other.

Since \(m,n<10000\), the pairs are
\[
(m,2m)\quad(m=1,\dots,4999)
\]
and
\[
(2n,n)\quad(n=1,\dots,4999).
\]
There are \(4999+4999=9998\) such ordered pairs.

\[
\boxed{9998}
\]
